# Monarchs of Denmark — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/danish-monarchs.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/danish-monarchs.ttl`](../decks/danish-monarchs.ttl) · **Cards:** 22 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The 22 monarchs of Denmark from Christian I, the first king of the House of Oldenburg (1448), to Frederik X, king since 14 January 2024, as of 4 October 2026. Front: the monarch's regnal name in English and Swedish; back: the years of the reign, counted from accession to death, deposition or abdication, with the royal house (Oldenburg or Glücksburg) and a short fact in a note. Taken from Wikidata (one note from the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica) and checked against the Danish Royal House's list of monarchs (kongehuset.dk), Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon, Nationalencyklopedin and the Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource, which is in the public domain (published before 1931; its article on Christian IV is by Robert Nisbet Bain, who died in 1909). The selection of monarchs, the reign years, the English and Swedish names, the royal houses and every fact in the notes come from Wikidata, except Christian IV's coming of age in 1596, which comes from the Britannica article, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Danish Royal House's website (all rights reserved), Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon (copyright, restricted reuse), Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts that the content sources gave, and no wording, table layout, name form, selection or fact was taken from them. The Royal House's differing years for three reigns are recorded only in the evidence and the quality-control log, where short quotations document the check. The selection is the complete line of Danish monarchs since 1448, which every list shares because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from any one list. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording of facts.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Finding the position: the Wikidata search API (query 6) returned Q18341329 "Monarch of Denmark" ("monarchical head of state of the Kingdom of Denmark").
3. Selection and reign years: query 1 fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service every non-deprecated P39 (position held) statement whose value is Q18341329, with its P580 (start time), P582 (end time), P1365 (replaces) and P1366 (replaced by) qualifiers, its rank, the holder's P53 (family) with the family's English and Swedish labels, and the holder's English and Swedish labels. The result runs from legendary kings to the present. The holders whose statement starts in 1448 or later are 22 people, Christian I (start 1448-10-07) to Frederik X (start 2024-01-14, preferred rank, no end time), each with one statement, linked into one unbroken chain by the replaces/replaced-by qualifiers; they became the cards. The back of each card is the year of P580 and the year of P582, joined by an en dash, and "2024–" for Frederik X, whose reign continues. No card's years come from anywhere else; the other sources only confirmed or differed (see quality control).
4. Note facts: query 2 fetched for the 22 statements the end-cause qualifier (P1534), the holder's father (P22) and date of birth (P569); query 2b Frederik X's mother (P25); query 3 the properties of the House of Oldenburg (Q155594), the House of Glücksburg (Q155616) and its Danish branch item (Q111201485); query 4 the holders' other positions (P39 Monarch of Sweden, Monarch of Norway) with their start and end and the date of death (P570). Every note fact but one is a Wikidata statement or follows directly from two of them (that Christian II was Frederick I's nephew: Frederick I and Hans are both sons of Christian I, Christian II is the son of Hans; that the throne was vacant from 1533 to 1534: Frederick I's statement ends in April 1533 and Christian III's starts in July 1534; that Christian IV was ten at his accession: born 1577-04-22, king from 1588-04-14). The notes are the compiler's own wording, written directly in English and in Swedish. The exception is Christian IV's coming of age in 1596, which Wikidata does not hold (query 4b found no P793 significant-event statement on Q153586): it comes from the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica article "Christian IV." by Robert Nisbet Bain on Wikisource (query 15 fetched the article pages, which only transclude the scanned pages; query 16 the transcribed page that holds the article's opening, "attaining his majority on the 17th of August 1596"; query 17 its licence box), and Lex ("Først 8 år senere i 1596 blev han kronet til dansk-norsk konge og dermed regent") and Nationalencyklopedin ("dröjde det till 1596 innan han blev myndig och kröntes") confirm it. The years that the Royal House's list gives where it differs from the cards (Hans, Christian III, Christian IV) are recorded in those cards' evidence and in quality control, not in the notes.
5. Names: the Wikidata API (query 5) fetched the English, Swedish, Danish and multilingual labels and aliases and the English, Swedish and Danish Wikipedia sitelinks of the 22 monarchs and the three house items. English fronts: the Wikidata English label or alias without "of Denmark". The Christians are Christian I–X. The Fredericks follow one rule: Frederick (the English form) for the seven kings of the House of Oldenburg, Frederik (the Danish form) for the three of the House of Glücksburg, as Wikidata's English labels and aliases have them (aliases "Frederick I" … "Frederick VII"; labels "Frederik VIII of Denmark", "Frederik IX of Denmark", "Frederik X of Denmark"), and as the English Wikipedia titles do except for Frederick VIII. King Hans is "Hans" in English too: his Wikidata English label is "John, King of Denmark" but his English alias, the English Wikipedia title ("Hans, King of Denmark") and the Royal House's English page all use Hans. Swedish fronts: the Wikidata Swedish label or alias without "av Danmark": Kristian I–X, Fredrik I–IX, Hans, Margrethe II and Frederik X. That is also how the Swedish Wikipedia list names every one of them, and Nationalencyklopedin writes Kristian IV, V, VI, VIII, IX, X, Fredrik IV, Fredrik IX ("danska Frederik IX"), Margrethe II and Frederik X (queries 12–13): Swedish keeps the Swedish forms Kristian and Fredrik for the historical kings but the Danish form Frederik for the present king, so the deck does too. The house names in the notes are the Wikidata labels: House of Oldenburg / Huset Oldenburg (Q155594), House of Glücksburg (Q155616) / huset Glücksburg (Q111201485, capitalised at the start of a note).
6. Official check: the Danish Royal House's English page "The Royal Lineage" was downloaded with curl and its text extracted with a small HTML-to-text script (query 7). It gives each monarch's years twice, in the entry heading and in the timeline; every card's years were compared with both. They agree for 19 monarchs; for Hans (1482–1513), Christian III (timeline 1534–1559, heading 1536–1559, and an interregnum 1533–1536) and Christian IV (1588/1596–1648) the page differs, see quality control. Its timeline shows "Frederik X — Since 2024", which together with Wikidata (no end time), Lex ("2024-", article last changed 15 September 2026) and Nationalencyklopedin ("kung av Danmark sedan 2024") confirms that Frederik X still reigned on 4 October 2026.
7. Independent check: the article "kongerækken i Danmark" in Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon (query 8) gives the years of every reign; it agrees with every card, including Hans 1481–1513, Christian III 1534–1559 (interregnum 1533–1534) and Christian IV 1588–1648. Its licence terms were read (query 9). The Swedish Wikipedia "Lista över Danmarks regenter" (query 10, wikitext of revision 59658833 through the MediaWiki API; query 11 for the licence footer) gives the Swedish name and the accession and end date of every reign; every card agrees with it. The comparison was done by reading the extracted texts side by side with the Wikidata CSV; each card's evidence quotes the row of each source.
8. Dossier: the script make_dossier.py (a working script, not published; everything it produced is in this dossier) wrote the first version of the cards. It holds a table with one row per monarch in order of accession: the card id, the English and Swedish fronts and the Wikidata label or alias each is checked against (chosen by the rule in the fifth step), the back (the P580 and P582 years read from q1.csv), and the readings of Lex, the Royal House's page and the Swedish Wikipedia typed in from the extracted texts; a second table holds each card's notes, written by hand from the facts listed in the fourth step, with the Wikidata statements they rely on, and a third the Nationalencyklopedin quotes. For each row it read the statement's start, end, rank and P53 houses from q1.csv and the label-or-alias kind and the sitelinks from names.json, and wrote the card, its evidence (the "says" texts) and its Wikidata checks. Later changes were made to the dossier directly and are logged under quality control. The 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource (query 15) was first considered for the note facts and set aside because its article pages only transclude scanned pages; in review round 3 the transcribed page for Christian IV was read (query 16) and supplies one note fact (fourth step).
9. Machine checks: every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: P39 = Q18341329 (the person held the position), P53 = the house named in the note (House of Oldenburg Q155594, House of Glücksburg Q155616 or its Danish branch item Q111201485, whichever the item holds), the English and Swedish front text as a label or alias (with the disambiguator where the front drops one), the house labels, and every statement a note relies on (P22, P25, P39 Monarch of Sweden / Norway, P569 and P570 years, P361, P53 of the neighbouring monarch, the aliases Kristian Tyrann, Johan II, Christian Frederick and Kristian Fredrik). The reign years are qualifiers, which the builder's checks cannot read; they rest on query 1 and the comparison in the sixth and seventh steps and are quoted in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

Every monarch of Denmark from Christian I, elected in 1448 as the first king of the House of Oldenburg, to Frederik X, king since 14 January 2024 and still reigning on 4 October 2026: 22 cards, among them one queen regnant, Margrethe II. A reign is counted from accession (succession on the predecessor's death or abdication, or election) to the monarch's death, deposition or abdication; coronations are not used (so Christian IV counts from 1588, not 1596), and only years are given. The throne was vacant between Frederick I's death in 1533 and Christian III's election in 1534; that interregnum gets no card. Left out: the monarchs before 1448 (Christopher of Bavaria and earlier, of other houses and, before Gorm the Old, of uncertain dates), regents who were not monarchs (Frederick VI as regent for his father from 1784 is not counted before 1808), and Christian VIII's and others' reigns in Norway and Sweden as cards of their own (they appear in notes). The years of the reigns of Hans, Christian III and Christian IV differ in some lists; the cards follow Wikidata, Lex and the Swedish Wikipedia, and the Royal House's differing figures are recorded in those cards' evidence.

## Queries

**1. Every P39 statement for Monarch of Denmark with start, end, replaces, replaced by, rank, house and labels (sh <scratch>/run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > q1.csv)** (Wikidata: the holders of the position Monarch of Denmark (Q18341329), with the start and end of each reign, their royal houses, parents and other positions, and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the monarchs and houses)

```
SELECT ?person ?en ?sv ?start ?end ?rank ?replaces ?replacedBy ?house ?houseEn ?houseSv WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q18341329 ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  FILTER(?rank != wikibase:DeprecatedRank)
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1365 ?replaces }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1366 ?replacedBy }
  OPTIONAL { ?person wdt:P53 ?house .
    OPTIONAL { ?house rdfs:label ?houseEn FILTER(LANG(?houseEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?house rdfs:label ?houseSv FILTER(LANG(?houseSv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start

```

**2. End cause, father and date of birth of the 22 monarchs (sh <scratch>/run.sh q2)** (Wikidata: the holders of the position Monarch of Denmark (Q18341329), with the start and end of each reign, their royal houses, parents and other positions, and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the monarchs and houses)

